# A read with no covering subscription is refused, with the fix

Registration refuses a template that reads something it never subscribes to, and
names the subscription entry that would cover it.

## An uncovered attribute reference

```yaml
name: uncovered-attribute-ref
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: producer
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          bar: {type: string, default: v}

  - type: receiver
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          copied:
            type: string
            source: "{{nodes.producer.attribute.bar}}"
```

`receiver` reads `producer` and subscribes to nothing.

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/templates" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$SPEC"
```

HTTP 400, no template id. The response carries a structured
`validation_errors` entry of kind `substitution_ref_uncovered`:

```json
{
  "kind": "substitution_ref_uncovered",
  "ref": "{{nodes.producer.attribute.bar}}",
  "receiver_node_type": "receiver",
  "attribute_property": ".../copied",
  "suggested_subscribes_entry": {
    "node": "producer",
    "type": "attribute/bar/changed",
    "force_upstream_refresh": false
  }
}
```

## The fix is the one shown

```yaml
  - type: receiver
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: producer
        type: attribute/bar/changed
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          copied:
            type: string
            source: "{{nodes.producer.attribute.bar}}"
```

Adding exactly that entry makes the same template register.

## An uncovered message reference

```yaml
name: uncovered-message-ref
version: "1"
messages:
  - type: orders/created
    body_schema:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: {type: string}
nodes:
  - type: receiver
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          oid:
            type: string
            source: "{{messages.orders/created.id}}"
```

Refused the same way, naming `{{messages.orders/created.id}}` and the entry
`{node: orders/created, type: terminal/success, force_upstream_refresh: false}`.

## Ask before registering

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/templates/validate" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$SPEC"
```

The same finding, with `ok: false`, before any registration is attempted. One
check reached from two places, not two checks that could drift.
